# Homes and home upgrades

## In short
- **House level is what keeps you alive at night.** If more zombies reach your house than your total home defense, you die.
- **One level per day.** You can raise your house one level per day (2–8 AP, plus resources at levels 2–8). In Pandemonium or a town in chaos there is no daily limit [1].
- **Heroes get extras.** Only heroes can build house extensions such as Reinforcements, Fence, Lock and Alarm. Heroes also get +2 house defense, and Guardians +3 [2].
- **Theft.** While you are in town, your chest cannot be robbed by normal thieves. When you are outside, only a lock protects it: the Lock extension, an item with the `lock` property such as Padlock and Chain, a `lock` house tag, or a house level with theft protection [3].

## How it works

### House levels
Each level gives a fixed amount of house defense. Costs depend on whether Urban plan (`small_urban_#00`) is built [4] [2].

| Lv | Name | Defense | AP (with Urban plan) | Resources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Camp Bed | 0 | 0 (0) | – |
| 1 | Tent | 1 | 2 (2) | – |
| 2 | Hovel | 4 | 4 (4) | Rotting Log |
| 3 | Shack | 9 | 5 (4) | Twisted Plank |
| 4 | House | 16 | 6 (5) | Wrought Iron |
| 5 | Safehouse | 25 | 6 (6) | Padlock and Chain, 2× Wrought Iron, 2× Twisted Plank, Patchwork Beam |
| 6 | Stronghold | 36 | 7 (6) | Boxes, 3× Wrought Iron, Sheet Metal (parts), 2× Twisted Plank |
| 7 | Bunker | 49 | 7 (7) | 2× Unshaped Concrete Blocks, Old Door, Handful of nuts and bolts, 6× Wrought Iron, Metal Support, Mini Hi-Fi (on) |
| 8 | Castle | 64 | 8 (8) | Car Door, 2× Unshaped Concrete Blocks, 2× Handful of nuts and bolts, 8× Wrought Iron, 2× Metal Support, 3× Sheet Metal (parts), 5× Twisted Plank, 3× Patchwork Beam |

**Upgrading the house level.** The game refuses the upgrade if any of these applies [1]:
- the town is devastated, or there is no next level;
- you are tired, or you have less AP than the cost (AP only, BP is not used);
- you already have the status `tg_home_upgrade` (already upgraded today). This check is skipped in chaos and in `panda` towns;
- the level's required construction is not complete;
- the resources are not in your chest plus your rucksack. With Urban plan, the Urban plan resource list is used instead.

When it succeeds:
- The new level is set, the AP is deducted and you get `tg_home_upgrade` [1].
- Each resource is consumed with its own chance, and you receive the picto `r_homeup_#00` [1].
- A town log entry is written unless `OptModifierHideHomeUpgrade` is set [1].

### House extensions (heroes only)
To build or level an extension [1]:
- You need a hero job and a house level that allows extensions, and the town must not be devastated.
- You need AP + BP at least equal to the cost. The tiredness check is commented out in the code.
- The cost is taken from AP first, then from CP.
- Resources come from your chest plus your rucksack, each consumed with its own chance.
- You receive the picto `r_hbuild_#00`.

Costs are given per level as [AP, items] [4]:

| Extension | Levels and costs | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Large Curtain (`curtain`) | 1: 4 AP | Others can't look into your house from the citizen list. Your chest can't be listed by others unless they have an active intrusion on you [5] [6] |
| Home Laboratory (`lab`) | 1: 6 AP + `machine_1_#00`; 2: 4 + `electro_#00`; 3: 4 + `tube_#00`; 4: 6 + `engine_#00` | +25% chance of a powerful drug per level (card text) |
| Kitchen (`kitchen`) | 1: 6; 2: 3 + `small_knife_#00`; 3: 4 + `machine_2_#00`; 4: 4 + `machine_3_#00` | +33% chance of a good dish per level (card text) |
| Rudimentary Alarm (`alarm`) | 1: 4 + `metal_#00` | Exposes intruders and thieves (see Theft) |
| Siesta Time™ (`rest`) | 1: 6; 2: 3 + `wood2_#00`; 3: 4 + `bed_#00` | +33% chance of sleeping soundly per level (card text) |
| Lock (`lock`) | 1: 6 + `chain_#00` | Theft protection |
| Fence (`fence`) | 1: 3 + `chain_#00` + `metal_beam_#00` | +3 home defense |
| More Storage (`chest`) | Levels 1–13 at 2, 2, 2, 3, 4, then 6 AP each | +1 chest slot per level |
| Reinforcements (`defense`) | Levels 1–4: 3 AP; levels 5–10: 6 AP. Levels 2–10 need `fence_#00`; levels 7–10 also need `metal_#00` | Defense = level up to level 6, then 6 + 2×(level − 6), so 14 at level 10 |

### Home defense formula
Home defense is the sum of the following parts [2] [7]:
- **House level defense.**
- **Fortifications** (`small_city_up_#00`): +4 when built.
- **Hero job:** +2. A Guardian gets +1 more.
- **Permanent extra defense** of the house. For example, installing a Makeshift Barricade adds +1 [8].
- **Temporary home defense** and **home-dump temporary defense.**
- **Reinforcements and Fence:** counted only if you are a hero.
- **Chest items:** +1 for each intact, non-poisoned defense item, and +2 for each `soul_blue_#00`, `soul_blue_#01` or `soul_red_#00`.

A dead citizen's house has 0 defense [2].

**Share counted in town defense.** Only house level + hero +2 + base upgrades count, multiplied by 0.4. The factor is 0.8 once Community Involvement (`small_strategy_#00`) is built [2] [9]. These parts do **not** count for the town: the Guardian +1, dump defense, chest items and souls [2].

### The nightly attack
- Each attacked citizen dies if the zombies at their house exceed their home defense.
- A survivor who is not already terrified (and when there is no Cinema) gets terror with this chance :
  - start at 100%;
  - minus `min(deco, 10)`;
  - −3 if clean (status `tg_clothes` or carrying `basic_suit_#00`);
  - −5 with `tg_home_clean`;
  - −10 with `tg_home_shower`;
  - −25 with `good_smell`;
  - −10 with Earplugs (`bquies_#00`) in the rucksack or chest.

### Decoration points
- Your decoration is the sum of the deco values of all unbroken items in your chest [3].
- Only the first 10 points reduce terror.
- The highest-value items are Chuck Figurine, unloaded Assault Rifle and Lit Pumpkin (15 each), then Persian Rug and the HiFis (10), and Teddy Bear (8) [list_entities item].

### Chest size
- Chest slots = 4 + chest-space bonus + More Storage level + additional storage [10].
- Additional storage comes from installed items: Boxes give +1 and the Iron Chest gives +2 [11] [12].

### Theft and intrusion
**When a house is protected** [3]:
- A dead citizen's house is never protected.
- A living citizen who is in town is protected, unless the thief has `EnableAdvancedTheft`.
- Explicit protections, which work even when the owner is outside:
  - a house level with theft protection;
  - the house tag `lock`;
  - the Lock extension;
  - an item with the `lock` property in the chest, such as Padlock and Chain `lock_#00` [13];
  - during Halloween, a `haunting_soul` in the chest against a thief it already scared.

**Starting an intrusion** [14]:
- The victim must be outside, unless the thief has advanced theft. Dead victims are always allowed.
- It is blocked if you have `tg_steal` (outside chaos), or, for stealing, if you have sent the victim an item by private message.
- With an Alarm, the intrusion is logged publicly and the victim gets a crow message, at most once every 15 minutes per intruder.

**Taking an item** [15]:
- Items with the `nosteal` property cannot be stolen.
- The thief gets `tg_steal` and the picto `r_theft_#00` (or `r_plundr_#00` from a dead citizen's house).
- Outcomes against a living victim are checked in this order:
  1. An Impersonal Exploding Doormat (`trapma_#00`) in the chest, or the `rabid_dog` house tag, wounds the thief, or kills them if already wounded. The theft is logged and the doormat is consumed.
  2. A Christmas or Leprechaun costume makes the theft anonymous.
  3. An Alarm always exposes the thief.
  4. Otherwise the thief is discovered with a **50%** base chance [16].
- Looting a dead citizen's house is always logged.
- The victim always gets a crow message.

**Putting an item into someone else's house:**
- It is discovered with a 10% chance, or always if they have an Alarm, unless you wear a costume [15].
- It is forbidden into a dead citizen's house or while the town is in chaos, and bag extensions can't be deposited [15].

## What changes it
- **Urban plan** (`small_urban_#00`): unlocks the alternative AP costs and resources for house levels [2] [4].
- **Fortifications:** +4 to every house. **Community Involvement:** house defense counts ×0.8 instead of ×0.4 in town defense [2].
- **Hero jobs:** +2 defense and access to extensions. **Guardian:** +1 more, at home only [2].
- **Hero skills:**
  - Enduring gives +1 or +2 chest slots (`props.bonus.chest_space`) [17] [18].
  - The legacy skills Large Chested and False Bottom each describe one extra chest slot [19] [20].
  - Strategist (`super_strategist_3`, 80 hero days) grants `features.advanced_theft`, which lets you steal from citizens who are in town [21].
- **Statuses `tamer_watch_1` / `tamer_watch_2`:** multiply the thief's discovery chance by 0.5 / 0.75, then both statuses are removed [15].
- **Home dump:** you can dump up to house level × 2 items at home. Your own rucksack items are only dumpable when your house level is above 0  [22].
- **Recycling a dead citizen's house:** only possible if its level is above 1. Default settings: 15 AP, return 5 [5] [23].

## Town types
- **Pandemonium (`panda`):**
  - no once-per-day limit on house upgrades [1];
  - `hide_home_upgrade` is true, so house upgrades are not logged [24];
  - Fortifications costs more there [25].
- **Chaos:** removes the daily house-upgrade limit and the `tg_steal` limit, but blocks putting items into other houses [1] [14].
- **Small, remote and custom:** no home-specific differences were found. Custom towns can change `OptModifierHideHomeUpgrade` and the recycling settings [26] [27].
